headline: FCC clears SpaceX's million-satellite orbital AI plan; shares sit below IPO price
bottomLine: The FCC conditionally approved SpaceX's Starmind orbital data-center plan, but SpaceX and Anthropic trade below IPO prices with Tesla merger talks and a Dec. 8 unlock ahead. Nvidia reinstated Huang after Trump lobbied, and 3.8% PCE inflation all but locks in a December Fed hike.

portfolio.title: FCC conditionally approves SpaceX's million-satellite Starmind data-center plan
portfolio.brief: The FCC authorized SpaceX's solar-powered Starmind constellation of up to 1 million satellites. Conditions: backup radio links, more safety data for higher orbits, and a 2040 deployment deadline.
portfolio.impact: First regulatory green light for orbital AI compute at scale, and the clearest support yet for moving AI power demand off the grid. The conditions mean years of engineering before any revenue.
portfolio.action: Ask SpaceX investor relations which FCC conditions gate the first Starmind launches and what capex that implies; bring the answer to the partner discussion before the Dec. 8 unlock.

portfolio.title: SpaceX and Anthropic trade below IPO prices as SpaceX unlock and Tesla merger loom
portfolio.brief: SPCX fell about 4% Tuesday and trades below its IPO price, as does Anthropic ($83). Tesla and SpaceX named five directors for merger talks, ratio unsettled; up to 797.6M SPCX shares unlock Dec. 8.
portfolio.impact: Merger terms, a Tesla vote and regulatory risk are all open while new supply arrives, so expect pressure into Dec. 8. Sub-IPO trading here and at Anthropic also chills the window for later listings.
portfolio.action: Set the sell/hold plan for the Dec. 8 unlock now, and confirm with fund ops what the first-20% sale already covered, before the plan goes to partners.

portfolio.title: xAI faces two state Grok suits, a California law fight and co-founder exits
portfolio.brief: Virginia and Oregon sued SpaceX and xAI over Grok sexualized images. xAI's appeal against California's AI disclosure law drew skeptical judges, and three co-founders launched startup Epochal.
portfolio.impact: Legal exposure now sits inside the SpaceX stake, and a lost disclosure appeal would set a template for other states. Founder departures raise the question of who runs the AI roadmap.
portfolio.action: Ask SpaceX's general counsel to size the Virginia/Oregon exposure and the California appeal timeline, and ask who now leads xAI product, before the Dec. 8 unlock.

portfolio.title: Erebor lends $100M+ to Harbinger and $50M to Forward Industries
portfolio.brief: Erebor and Pinegrove gave truck maker Harbinger over $100M in debt; Erebor separately made Forward Industries a $50M two-year loan. Its loans have passed $1B against about $7B in deposits.
portfolio.impact: Erebor is turning startup deposits into a loan book, the first evidence of how it earns a spread. Loans are still a small slice of deposits, so loan growth is the profitability test.

portfolio.brief: Back in a lower court, Amazon wants to continue its suit over Perplexity's AI shopping agent; Bloomberg Law says the judge looked divided. Perplexity also launched a Monitor API.
portfolio.impact: The outcome decides whether platforms can block third-party agents, the core risk for Perplexity's push into agentic products like Computer. A loss could narrow where its agents may operate.
portfolio.action: Ask Perplexity's general counsel for the next hearing date and how a ruling for Amazon would change the Computer and Teammates roadmap, ahead of the next partner call.

regulation.next: Congress returns after Thanksgiving; chip-curb bills and Nvidia's board inquiry are the next markers.

regulation.title: South Korea drafts bank-led stablecoin rules and plans to lift 2017 ICO ban
regulation.brief: The FSC draft limits won-stablecoin issuance to bank-majority consortia and caps exchange ownership at 20%, with exceptions. It would also let domestic projects sell tokens under IPO-style disclosure rules.
regulation.impact: Korea reopens a large retail market to token issuance but hands stablecoins to banks, favoring regulated issuers over crypto natives. That rewards tokens with disclosed revenue.
regulation.next: Draft Digital Asset Act needs lawmakers' approval; no timetable in reports.

regulation.title: White House seeks funding exemptions for Golden Dome in next stopgap bill
regulation.brief: The White House asked for exemptions so Golden Dome and a Trump battleship can be funded in the next stopgap. It warned the Pentagon's munitions ramp-up could face turmoil without key-program approvals.
regulation.impact: A stopgap without exemptions freezes new starts and slows awards for fast-scaling suppliers like Anduril; approval would keep missile and munitions work moving.
regulation.action: Ask Anduril how a stopgap without program exemptions would delay its awards and production plans, and get its answer before the next appropriations vote.
regulation.next: Next stopgap bill is the vehicle; exemption approval is still pending.

tech.action: Ask Super Protocol and Aizel Network how their confidential-compute and TEE products would serve labs if training-monitoring standards are adopted; get answers next week.

frontier.title: Physicists trap and cool a positron in a wall-free trap
frontier.brief: Researchers trapped a positron, the electron's antimatter twin, and cooled it near absolute zero, suspended away from ordinary matter. Reported via ScienceDaily; peer review and the lab are not stated.
frontier.impact: A step toward precision tests of matter-antimatter symmetry, which probe whether the Standard Model explains why matter dominates. Treat as an early lab result until a paper and replication appear.
